text:
maya: quick q — ran into a case where a feature flag (product LD) and a console rollout policy both define traffic for the same canary. which source should win? behavior looked inconsistent across regions.

jordan: we don't have a documented single-source rule today, which is why it surprises folks.

sam: fwiw current runtime merge logic is basically timestamp-based: last write wins, which mixes console API writes, runtime autoscaler writes, and flag syncs. messy.

lin: for safety we purposely wanted console to be able to do an emergency kill switch. that seems like it needs higher precedence.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: applied canary rollout service-x @2026-03-15T12:04Z (5% -> 20%) :rocket:

maya: concrete example — console rollout set global allocation to 10% (canary group=flag A), but feature-flag the product team toggled for a cohort to 0% to block an experiment. some users still got routed because runtime merged differently.

jordan: here is what we have in code (pseudo):
```
# merge heuristic (pseudocode)
if rollout_policy and feature_flag:
    use whichever write_ts is later
elif rollout_policy:
    apply rollout_policy
else:
    apply feature_flag
```

sam: timestamp heuristics are brittle because syncs happen from multiple controllers. we should instead have a deterministic precedence matrix.

lin: proposal: make "safety" signals (console emergency) top priority, then runtime policies, then app-level flags. that guarantees ops can kill traffic quickly.

maya: i worry about over-prioritizing console for targeting nuance; product flags should be able to target cohorts finer-grained than console rollouts. maybe separate decision surfaces: allocation vs targeting guards.

jordan: i like that — split the problem. allocation = how many tokens/requests go to variant; targeting = which users are eligible. precedence can differ per decision.

sam: sketch of precedence table:
```
# decision   | precedence (high -> low)
allocation    | console_rollout > runtime_policy > feature_flag
targeting     | runtime_policy > feature_flag > console_rollout
guards        | runtime_policy > console_rollout > feature_flag
```

lin: that seems reasonable but we need to keep it simple to explain to support oncall. also need a visible resolution path in the Console UI — show which source won and why.

maya: agreed. actionability: can we add source metadata to the routing decision trace and dashboards? so oncall can quickly see "console override" vs "flag override".

jordan: yes — we can add a `decision.source` field to traces and to per-request logs. also include the effective allocation and contributing sources.

sam: immediate short-term fix: make console emergency kill-switch (a specific flag) always win for allocation decisions. longer term: RFC to formalize the matrix and implement explainability in runtime + console.

incident-bot: incident-bot: RFC-342 opened: "Rollout vs Feature-Flag Precedence and Explainability" — tracker #RFC-342

lin: can we also add a runtime warning when conflicting configs detected? like a noisy alert if both feature-flag and rollout set allocations for same resource.

maya: yes please. add an alert and a little UI banner: "conflicting allocation: console and feature-flag both set — see resolution" with link to the RFC once merged.

jordan: i'll draft the RFC with the matrix + migration plan. sam, lin — can you enumerate current code paths that write allocations and timestamps? want to map all sources.

sam: on it. will also prototype the `decision.source` field format: {source: "console_rollout", id: "rollout-123", confidence: "forced"}

lin: thumbs up. if we agree, short-term change: emergency kill-switch in console = immediate override + trace flag. longer term: show precedence in UI and make logs explain which source decided.

maya: sounds good. thanks all :thumbsup: 

jordan: added a checklist to RFC-342: (1) emergency override behavior, (2) decision-source telemetry, (3) conflict alerting, (4) UI explain panel, (5) migration plan for existing timestamp-based merges.

maya: great. feel free to @me on the RFC when draft is up.
